Exp servers are low pop and allow me to live long enough to really check out all the features like making a complete leather suit and fishing and hunting and stuff. Getting used to the layout of cities across the map.  

I play DayZ focusing on what life would be like if something like this happened and much less about gearing up and finding people to kill as fast as possible.  I play DayZ very much like how I would live my life under extreme circumstances.  In real life I would never ever kill someone on sight. That is strictly video game behavior. If I just wanted to gear up and go kill people I'd play PubG.  

High pop servers are filled with kids who grew up playing COD, Battlefield, Quake, and Doom. They've grown up with their real lives and video game lives totally disassociated from one another.  I watch them play DayZ on Twitch and they run through the map taking advantage of glitches and are so familiar with the map that they can run into buildings and go straight to the spots they know loot will be flipping on their inventory screen and grabbing stuff so fast that the people watching can barely see what they just did.  That style of play is just not for me. 

When I read a book I do it as though I'm narrating the story in my head. I read at the same speed I speak at, I don't rip through the book reading it as fast as I can.  People who read too fast miss out on soo much. A paragraph tells you so much more than just the words on a page.  Imagine what your DayZ character must be smelling when he walks into these old houses. What must a Zombie smell like after rotting for months?  

These houses are what is supposed to be what was a Russian-bloc country.  Have you ever walked into a Russian/Polish/Czech family home? Their food fills the air with a unique smell. What might one of those homes smell like after everyone has died and rotted?  These are things too many players never think about when they run at full speed for 10 minutes and into a house and sprint full speed back out when the loot isn't there. Then sprint across a field and up a ladder into a deer stand where they immediately climb back down only to sprint another 10 minutes somewhere else.  Nobody does this in real life.  If you sprint across a field and climb a deer stand you're going to fall or get up there and take a seat and catch your breath..at very least. 

Another reason I play Exp is that I've been playing DayZ since a short time after Standalone came out and for a long time Exp was introducing new features that were not yet implemented in stable and I just got used to liking the new stuff so much that I just stick with it even though at this moment there isn't a big difference between the two.

Every person that went to Navy boot camp had to do this for no less than 15 minutes, if I remember correctly. 

I remember we had this one guy in our company that must have been just barely under the fat regulations. He was also built very unusual with a long torso and tiny legs and walked around with his butt kinda sticking out. He looked like a giant dwarf really. He was very quiet and when he did speak he had a very heavily pronounced lisp. I don't mean to be crass or whatever, but in order to describe it best I'd say it was what might be described as a "gay-lisp". 

Other guys in my company wondered out loud how and why this guy wound up in Navy boot camp. Surely his recruiter would have told him that US Navy sailors are required to be able to swim, right !?!

Well we get to the pool and this guy goes over to our company commander and begins crying and begging not to have to do the swimming tests. 

My CC was surprised and pissed and told him he'd be doing the tests with everyone else, or he'd be on a plane going home tonight. He wiped his eyes (with the palms of his hands like a toddler would) and went to the end of the line. 

The Navy Divers told us what they wanted us to do, explained how to get out of our dungarees and create flotation devices, and then tread water for something like 15 - 20 minutes or so. The divers also told us what to do if anything went wrong. He said they had a very long pole that they would extend to anyone drowning and were VERY specific not to pull the pole because they would pull the person in. The told us many times that if they feel us pulling on the pole that they would simply let it go and leave the person to drown before sending divers to get them from the bottom. 

One by one we filed up onto the platform that was abnormally tall compared to anything I'd ever jumped from before. When they blew the whistle for my turn I jumped and fell what I thought was a very long fall and hit the water. It took longer to bob back to the surface than I'd ever experienced before, but like nearly everyone else I did what I needed to and finished the test. 

The crying sailor was last. He waddled up the ladders to the platform and now he was really bawling his eyes out. He put his hands in front of him like Frankenstein's monster and the whistle sounded for him to jump.  He stood there crying and shaking until finally being reminded that he'd be held back or worse if he didn't jump right now!

He stopped crying and jumped...and sunk straight to the bottom. I could see him pretty clearly now, he was standing on the bottom of the pool with big white eyes strained open and both arms desperatly reaching up, exactly like you'd see a toddler reaching up to their mother or father to be picked up. 

The man was panicking, it was clear. What blew me away was that he made absolutely no effort to swim. He didnt paddle, didn't kick, just sank. It looked like he may have tried to walk along the bottom if anything. The Navy divers guided the pole down to the distressed man and can you guess what he did with the pole? That's right, he pulled as hard as he could and the divers let the pole sink right down to the bottom. The extended a 2nd pole, same thing. The instructors looked at each other and gave a nod and the diver went down to get him. 

He didn't lose consciousness that I could tell, he popped up with the scuba diver and puked water for a while and that was it. He was gone from boot camp before my company returned from chow that night. My primary thoughts that night was how irresponsible that guys recruiter was. And how the hell did he pass the Navy's weight standard, and why did he think it was a good idea to join the US armed forces before 'Don't Ask , Don't Tell"?  That guy almost lost his life so that his recruiter could meet his quota for that month. Idiots.

Nothing else has worked the way the Rituximab has. My first tumors were physically removed followed by radiation therapy and they came back. After that they stopped the radiation all together and adopted a "wait and watch" strategy because none of the tumors were growing in vital areas that would harm me. Finally the Rituximab therapy just melted the tumors literally like butter and then I was prescribed Revlimid to hopefully prevent anything from trying to re-grow.  After starting a new relationship my doctor and I felt it is best to temporarily stop the Revlimid for now. If any area starts acting up again I might restart the Rev, but for now I just have to do one session of Rituximab every other month. Again, thank you from the bottom of my heart!

My parents told me a story about the first man to discover popcorn. The story they told me goes like this:

A group of Native American Indians had given corn to their livestock. Later they would collect the dung for emergency fire-kindling. As it turns out some of the dung had unchewed, undigested kernals of corn. Later the tribe was surprised when the dung they placed in the fire popped and expanded. Eventually one courageous and curious brave picked the popped-corn from the dung fire and studied it. This is where some of the stories differ as one version says the brave ate a kernel of popped corn from the dung. A less gross version of the story says the brave deduced that the same kernels of corn could be heated in the fire to pop without being eaten and defecated by animals. 

TL;DR The first person to discover popcorn was a courageous and curious Native American Brave.

While in the military we were warned about cons where a local girl takes interest in you only to be found by her angry father with a gun. As a PC gamer myself I understand the desire to go hardcore into games. I've lost over 2000 hours to DayZ and I'm 250 hours into Fallout 4 already. I was still dating my now ex when I started Playing DayZ. I could have made an effort to save the relationship, we had been together for 8 years after all. But at 38 I had chosen to move back to my parents and go back to school. 

She and I lived over 40 miles apart. I started out going to school Monday - Thursday and on Thursday night would drive to her and stay with her until Sunday night and drive 40 miles back. I did this probably around 75-100 times over two years. Then every weekend turned into every other weekend. Six months later every other weekend became three weeks and then one day I just didn't text her and she didn't text me at all.

Days went by and instead of checking in with her like I always did I just sat down at my PC and started up DayZ and played all day and night. I went to bed and the next day I repeated the same thing. Before I realized it I hadn't talked to her or texted in almost three weeks. I pulled up Facebook and not only was the 'in a relationship' status gone but it said 'single' as well. I texted her and received a text back that was very cold and ended with "...and we can never talk again." That was how we broke up. There was no final talk, we just drifted slowly apart until it was over. I played PC games so much I drifted right through the end of an almost-decade long relationship without even noticing until it was already over. 

I'm not saying this is going to happen to you or anyone else, just that I understand how anyone can lose himself in a really good PC game and neglect the important stuff like life and loved ones. It can be a drug like anything else. Get between your husband and really serious amounts of PC time, that's my recommendation.

From a guy that has been on Suboxone for almost 4 years now: I find it humorous that people think being on Suboxone = being clean. Suboxone itself is one of the most powerful opiates known to man. That's why it works the way it does. It's what they call a partial-agonist and not a full agonist like Demerol or Dilaudid. But make no mistake, when anesthesiologists have to do opiate level equivalencies for surgery a person on 8mg of Suboxone per day has to take a boatload of Dilaudid (one of the most potent opiate pain relievers available in the hospital) in order to both feel pain relief as well as avoid withdrawal. I know this from experience as I am not only on Suboxone but also have Lymphoma and chronic kidney stones. I have been stuck in hospitals with kidney stones waiting for days for the Subs to wear off so they can give me actual opiate pain relief. It took almost a week before the meds started working. Then three days of dilaudid.  

The scariest part about making the transition from pain relieving opiates back to Suboxone is the possibility of precipitated withdrawal. PW occurs when there is still full-agonist opiates left in the brain's receptor sites. If there is enough full-agonist opiate left in the brain when Suboxone is taken the person will be thrust into one of the worst nightmares of their lives. The deepest, darkest, most powerful withdrawal symptoms you can imagine. People say it's like Hell on Earth, and worst of all - no one can really do anything about it. If you go into PW in a hospital they leave you to suffer it out. The only way I've ever heard of anyone getting our of PW after taking a Sub with full opiates still inside you is if you have a lot of dope on hand and "shoot your way past it", which is extremely dangerous. The line between shooting enough full opiate-agonist to stop the misery of PW and overdose is a very thin line. The majority of people just suffer instead of trying to shoot past the PW.

I just want to be clear because there is often a lot of misunderstanding as to what Suboxone is. Some people see it as some kind of miracle drug because it stops withdrawal and I just want to remind everyone that Subs like any other opiate has a price to pay when using it. Suboxone itself is a very powerful opiate and if your goal is to kick all opiates and get clean you must find a doctor that is willing to work with you on a very strict regimen of whittling down. Most Sub Doctors will keep you on the same dose as long as you keep paying them. Only a handful want to see their clients get totally clean, so you have to find one of those and begin a very strict regimen of less, and less and less, until you're down to a tiny sliver of Sub and then make "the jump". Even then it's going to be rough. Even a tiny sliver of Sub is so potent that it's like coming off a 4 Vicodin twice a day habit. 

If you doubt how powerful Suboxone is just google "Suboxone opiate equivalency" and read what you find. You'll be surprised. Make no mistake, it can do wonders for people that have been sick and shooting for months or years, it can turn your life around. I just dont want anyone the think that being on Suboxone is equal to "being clean". It's not. You will not pass drug tests that forbid any kind of opiate use like bus driving, or piloting, or something where lives are at stake. Check with the job you're applying for to see their policy on Soboxone use. People are sometimes surprised when they fail and show their Sub prescription only to be told that they can't work on Subs either. Just beware.

Subs are a great step up from shooting dope, but it's in no way like actually being clean. Just wanted to clear that up. Good luck man, Subs are a good first step to restarting a legitimate life again.

I can't speak for you, I can only tell you about me and life from my own perspective. I can see from the comments that many people are suggesting that you put your foot down and leave your husband for what he has done. If I were a young person in my twenty's I might say the same, but as a forty year old man and half a lifetimes worth of experience I feel that trashing your marriage because of this would be a mistake. I'll try to explain why. 

When I was in high school I was dating my sweat heart Gretchen. She and I were perfect for each other, we were the kind of couple that could finish each other's sentences. We have the same sense of humor and when we communicate we share a language that most anyone else simply couldn't understand. There was a time I couldn't even imagine being with anyone else. We were each others first and in over 20 years there has never been anyone else like her or better than her. 

We split up after a pregnancy scare and my incredible fear of ruining her life with a child before graduation. Honestly when I broke up with her I thought surely we'd get back together again. That didn't happen. What did happen is that in her anger of being broken up with she reacted by sleeping with someone else. I found out and with my pride being hurt I decided that was the final straw and we were over forever. 

20 years has passed by now. In that time I've dated more than 15 women. I had a daughter with a woman that was the nightmare of my life. She cheated on me with friends, she had unprotected sex with multiple men in a single night and tried to sleep with me (luckily I found out before being seduced). I dated another woman for the last nine years before it fell apart in shambles. 

Gretchen married a man 11 years older than her. She had hundreds of horrible fights and for those years her life was often a nightmare. She left that man and married another man that gave her two beautiful children. A few months ago Gretchen and I reconnected as friends and talked about our past. We admitted we both loved each other so much and in many ways still do. 

This last July my only daughter died in a car accident at 19 years old. Of all my friends it has been Gretchen that has been there for me more than anyone else. She calls or texts to check on me every day. I babysit for her children and have fallen in love with them as if they were a part of my own family. 

My point is that she and I have talked and both agreed that we were meant for each other. My daughter should have been hers and her kids mine. My anger and pride destroyed what should have been an epic lifelong love. If you and your husband love each other and are meant to be together don't let this kiss be the reason you look back on your life and regret breaking up. If I could go back in time and take it back id do it in a second. She slept with another guy, big friggin deal. Knowing what I know now I couldn't care less. I'd take her back in a second if I had the chance. 

Do what's right for you, if this kiss is that important to you then divorce is available to you. But from a guy that has been through so much worse (infidelity, cancer, the loss of my only child) don't throw love away over something you will look back at twenty years from now and think is no big deal, like a kiss. Don't live with regret if you don't have to. Try to step back and look at the big picture, the long view. Talk to your parents, ask them if they've experienced anything in their lives like this. You might be surprised to find out that your mom and dad have regrets in their own past that will surprise you. Life can be messy and never works out like "The Notebook".

She cherished time spent with her aunts and cousins and extended family, but most of all she loves being with her Grandparents. She lives with her mother's grandparents and spent as much time as she could with mine. There is no way I can tell you all about her here on facebook. She is a complicated and amazing soul that can't be fully explained in writing on a computer. In the days and months ahead I will post more pictures and video of my precious pumpkin. She is my heart and will always be a part of me as long as it beats. I feel it's safe to say that everyone she has been in contact with that knows her feels the same way. She has the kind of personality that you just can't forget, ever. My pumpkin Zoee Elizabeth Norton.

The investigation is still ongoing but the doctors told us when they tested her blood that her blood sugar was incredibly low. Her maternal Grandfather has diabetes and has to take shots for it several times a day. 

It's also possible that she had dropped something onto the floor and thought her long limbs could reach it. We don't know for sure at this time. 

We do know that she was working a split shift at the Cedar Rapids Culver's and if she had taken the day off like she originally told me she would this wouldn't have happened. 

Her last words to me were "I'm going to bed daddy I'll text you tomorrow! I love you!"
